scorecard.note: Make the data graphics ultra‑simple (big numbers, clear arrows) so they stay legible on a small phone screen.

storyboard.ears: For years, the way we put babies to bed was killing them.
SIDS deaths fell to 0.64 per thousand babies, less than half the 1991 rate. One simple change in how babies sleep did that.
storyboard.evidence: CDC / NICHD | US SIDS rate per 1,000 live births, before vs. after Back to Sleep | https://safetosleep.nichd.nih.gov/about/history | 2026-10-06

storyboard.ears: Before the campaign, over 85% of SIDS cases were babies put down on their stomachs. Flipping them onto their backs did the trick.
storyboard.eyes: substance: the sleeping baby; cause: Data lifts the face-down baby and places it on its back in the crib
storyboard.evidence: CDC / NICHD (Safe to Sleep) | Share of SIDS cases where the baby was placed stomach-down vs. back-up, before vs. after the campaign | https://safetosleep.nichd.nih.gov/about/history | 2026-10-06

storyboard.ears: About 3,400 babies still die in sleep-related deaths every year. The danger is smaller, not gone, so the back still matters.
storyboard.evidence: CDC | Sleep-related infant deaths still recorded in the US each year | https://www.cdc.gov/sids/data.html | 2026-10-06

storyboard.ears: Know a new parent? Tell them: back to sleep. It costs nothing and it works.
